newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Foreign investment in Taiwan down 16 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Taiwan down 16 pct in 1996.

text.p: Foreign investment in Taiwan fell 16 percent in 1996 to US$2.461 billion from $2.925 billion in 1995, due mainly to lower investment in the semiconductor industry, the state Investment Commission said on Friday.

Despite the decline, foreign investment in 1996 was still the second highest in history, surpassed only by 1995 when it jumped 79 percent from 1994 due to sharp increases in investment in the high-tech industry and Taiwan's active promotion of its regional operation centre scheme, the state commission said.

Foreign investment in the electronics and electrical appliance industries, which topped the investment sector with 18 percent of the pie, accounted for $443 million, down 64.3 percent from 1995 due to reduced investment in semiconductors amid an industry recession, it said.

But investment in other four major emerging industries -- finance and insurance, services, retail and international trade -- rose 22.9, 32.5, 118 and 8.3 percent, respectively, indicating rising foreign interest in Taiwan, it said.
Investment from unspecified "other" regions leapt 456 percent to $1.01 bilion, followed by investment from Japan which fell 4.0 percent to $545 million.
Investment from the United States plunged 63 percent to $474 million. Investment from Hong Kong surged 135 percent to $232 milion, but investment from Europe fell 41 percent to $197 million.
Taiwan's own overseas investment, excluding mainland China, surged 59 percent in 1996 to $2.16 billion from $1.36 billion a year earlier, it said in the same statement.
Indirect investment in China rose 12 percent to $1.229 billion despite Taipei's go-slow appeals to reduce political exposure in the rival mainland, the commission said.
The number of China projects fell 22 percent to 383. Such investments must be routed through Hong Kong or a third country.
Investment in unspecified "other" regions -- mainly tax havens in central America -- jumped 67 percent to $1.31 billion, followed by the United States, which rose 7.0 percent to $266 million.
Investment in southeast Asian nations surged as some Taiwan businesses have heeded Taipei's appeal to diversify their investments away from mainland China to other areas, it said.

Worried that Taiwan could become too dependent on rival China, Taiwan launched a "southbound policy" in 1993 to promote investments in Southeast Asia instead of China. A new appeal in 1996 urged Taiwan firms to invest at home, not the mainland.
Investment in Singapore leapt 421 percent to $165 million, followed by investment in Vietnam, which fell 7.0 percent to $100.5 million.
Investment in Malaysia, Indonesia, Phillipines, and Thailand surged 39, 158, 108 and 39 percent, respectively, it said.
Overseas investments focused on finance and insurance -- mainly in setting up investment holding companies -- electronics and electrical appliance, and transport industries, it said.
